resources.string: Connects Helper Application to Mes Validation for call recording. Enable this in Accessibility. Do not enable the accessibility shortcut.
Helper Application needs these permissions to be able do the following:
to allow the app to record calls
to detect incoming and outgoing calls
to detect whether a Bluetooth headset is active during a recording
Helper Application battery usage should not be optimized by your phone\'s built-in or third-party optimizer. Otherwise, you might not get the option to record calls.
Helper Application needs Mes Validation Connection enabled in Accessibility to detect calls and send them to the Mes Validation app for recording.
ATTENTION! Do NOT enable the shortcut option of the service. Unintentional touches on it can cause instability of the app.
Go to Accessibility > Installed / Downloaded apps > Call OS Helper > turn ON Mes Validation Connection (main switch, not the shortcut).

ACR-style (default): speakerphone + mic during calls — same as Cube ACR Helper Accessibility. Optional: Shizuku or MediaProjection below.

Default — same as Cube ACR Helper without Shizuku: turns on speakerphone during calls so the microphone picks up both sides. Keep volume audible; use speaker or earpiece at normal level.

Not required for ACR-style recording. For advanced capture: install Shizuku from Play Store (moe.shizuku.privileged.api), start it via wireless debugging, then grant permission here. NLL Store Shizuku is optional (only if you use ACR Phone Helper with that fork).

Try: Settings → Apps → Shizuku + Call OS Helper → Battery → Unrestricted. In Shizuku tap Start, then tap RETRY below. Logcat: package moe.shizuku.privileged.api, search ShizukuServiceStarter.

Until privileged recorder works: enable Speaker boost (above) for audible one-sided capture.

Records call playback + your mic (no loudspeaker). Tap Enable → Next → Start on the system screen. If the dialer opens, press Home and return here. Rebuild the app for a simpler “entire screen only” prompt. Keep Mes Validation Connection ON.

Two-way recording needs Android's "Share screen" permission (call audio only).

1. Tap Continue
2. Tap Next → Start (entire screen — do not pick apps)
3. If the Phone/dialer opens anyway, press Home and open Call OS Helper again
4. Check: "Two-way mode ON"

To avoid this flow, use Speaker boost instead.
If the dialer opened after you picked Phone, press Home → open Call OS Helper. If status is not ON, tap Enable again (new builds use entire screen only).
Status: Two-way mode OFF — mic-only fallback

Headset/earphone was connected during the call. Your voice is recorded from the mic; the other person\'s voice usually plays only in the headset, so it is missing. For two-way: unplug headset, enable speaker boost, and use loudspeaker (same as Cube ACR).
Only your voice was captured. On this Samsung build, two-way playback is blocked. Turn ON Speaker boost, unplug headset, use loudspeaker, and test again (AMR path).
Two-way is ON but Samsung blocked remote call audio in playback capture. Use Speaker boost + loudspeaker for both voices, or try Cube ACR on the same phone.
Recording — tap SPEAKER in Phone app (both voices)
Your voice was saved. For the other person: during the call open Phone app and tap Speaker (loudspeaker), volume high, no headset. Rebuild app uses MIC source when speaker boost is on.
Saved with audio. If you still hear only yourself, reinstall this update (uses VOICE_COMMUNICATION + speaker probe) and test with loudspeaker at high volume.

There are no unsent records. Everything is OK.
Call OS Helper is ready. Calls are saved to Documents/MesValidationCallRecorder. On most phones only the microphone is allowed — use speakerphone if playback is silent.
Setup is complete. Open Mes Validation to use full recording, or continue using local recording in this app.

Call recording depends on your phone model and Android version. This app uses the same approach as Cube ACR Helper — it works on many devices, but not all. Use this guide if audio is missing, quiet, or one-sided.
Does this work on every phone?

No. Android blocks full two-way call capture for normal apps on many phones (especially Samsung, Xiaomi, Realme, Android 10–16). You may hear both sides with speaker + mic, only your voice, or silence. That is a platform limit, not a bug in this app alone.
I hear both sides but the other person is quiet — is that normal?

Yes, on the standard (ACR-style) path that is common. The remote voice comes through the loudspeaker and is picked up by the microphone, so it is often softer than yours. Try: Recording settings → Phone calls clarity → MAX, Maximize in-call volume ON, use loudspeaker during the call, and increase phone volume.
I only hear myself on the recording

1) Enable Mes Validation Connection in Accessibility.
2) Recording settings → Phone audio source → Voice recognition (software).
3) Turn ON Maximize in-call volume and use loudspeaker (no headset).
4) Set Phone auto-recording delay to 4 seconds.
5) Force in-communication mode ON (turn OFF if caller becomes too quiet).
6) Unplug wired/Bluetooth headset.
How can I make the other person louder?

Use speakerphone at high volume during the call. In Recording settings set clarity improvement to MAX and Maximize in-call volume ON. Avoid headsets — they route remote audio to your ears only, not the mic.
What is Shizuku and when should I use it?

Shizuku gives this app elevated audio access without full root on many devices. If ACR-style recording is one-sided or silent, install Shizuku from Play Store, start it via wireless debugging, grant permission in Helper status, then test again. This is the recommended advanced path before rooting.
Do I need to root my phone?

Usually no — try Shizuku first. Root is only for users who accept security risk and still cannot record after Shizuku + all ACR settings. Rooting voids warranty and may break banking apps. We do not provide root instructions; use at your own risk.

Samsung often blocks line-level capture. Use speakerphone, keep Helper unrestricted in battery settings, enable Mes Validation Connection, and try Shizuku. If Shizuku privileged recorder fails to bind, use speaker boost path (you may get both sides at different volumes).
Laws vary by country and state. You must inform the other party and get consent where required. You are responsible for compliance. See Terms & conditions in the menu.

Telephone call recording is regulated differently worldwide. You agree to follow all laws in your jurisdiction and the callee\'s jurisdiction. Always notify participants that the call is being recorded when required by law.

Call OS Helper does not guarantee that any call will be recorded, that both sides will be captured, or that audio quality will meet your expectations. Android OEM restrictions vary by device, OS version, and carrier.

The app supports an ACR-style path (Accessibility + microphone/speaker routing) on many phones. Some devices only capture your microphone. Some produce silent files. Compatibility lists are illustrative only — your device may differ even from similar models.

Follow FAQ & troubleshooting: verify permissions, Mes Validation Connection, Recording settings (audio source, delay, speaker boost). Contact support with device model and Android version. The developer is not liable for OEM blocks.
Optional Shizuku integration requires a third-party app and user setup. You are responsible for Shizuku security and permissions. Shizuku may be blocked on some OEM builds despite correct setup.

Rooting or modifying system software is entirely your choice and risk. This app does not require root. We do not endorse rooting. Damage, data loss, or security issues from root are your responsibility.
Recordings are stored locally in Documents/MesValidationCallRecorder unless you enable backup features. You control sharing and deletion. Do not upload or share recordings unlawfully.
By using Call OS Helper you accept these terms. If you do not agree, disable recording and uninstall the app. Continued use after updates constitutes acceptance of revised terms.
